To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Meteor is an automatic translation quality evaluation metric which is designed with the explicit objective of producing sentence-level quality scores which correlate well human judgments, that this goal has been achieved, and that Meteor is the best automatic translation metric in terms of this correlation.

Meteor is the best-performing automatic metric for translation quality evaluation, that it has been used by many different research groups, and that it has been adopted as a standard metric for the Wmt evaluation campaign.

Meteor is the best available metric for automatic evaluation in the sense of correlation with human judgments, that it is the best performing metric for the evaluation of English–French translation, and that it performs well on other language combinations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of metrics for the automatic evaluation of machine translations.
the automatic evaluation of machine translated texts.
the design of metrics that are useful for machine translation research and development, and we believe that the design decisions incorporated into Meteor are important in this context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Meteor performs very well, but it is not perfect.
Meteor is the best automatic metric for evaluating machine translation output, and that it is a significant improvement over Bleu.
Meteor has been demonstrated to be one of the best automatic evaluation metrics available for MT systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Meteor has proven to be an effective metric for machine translation evaluation and has been widely adopted by both researchers and developers in the field.

Meteor has been shown to be the most accurate metric for MT evaluation in several recent evaluations, including those conducted by the European Language Resources Association (Elra) and the Association for Machine Translation in the Americas (Amta).
Meteor has consistently performed as well as or better than Bleu, and in several evaluations has outperformed all other metrics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Meteor metric has been successfully applied to the evaluation of machine translation in many different contexts, with high correlations with human judgments in a variety of language directions and with a variety of different types of human assessments.
Meteor is a reliable and robust metric for automatic evaluation that can be tuned for different types and sources of human judgments and that can be used in different language pairs.
